newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian government bond prices rally on easy call.
newsitem.headline: Indian government bond prices rally on easy call.

text.p: Indian securities prices rose sharply by 10 to 15 basis points for short-dated as well as medium-term papers on Thursday, dealers said.
"Lenders with excess funds shifted from call money market to security market," a dealer said.
The securities prices opened steady but rose by 15 basis points on short-dated securities towards the close on improved sentiments, dealers said.
The volume on the National Stock Exchange rose to 2.38 billion rupees on Thursday, compared to Wednesday's 1.88 billion rupees, a dealer said.
The 13.40 percent 1999 stock was in limelight, with a total volume of 400 million rupees, which rose by 28 basis points to 100.98 rupees against its previous close, dealers said.
The 13.55 percent 2001 stock rose by 23 basis points to 100.90 rupees compared to the previous close.
In treasury bills, June 1997 maturity paper was traded at a yield of 9.10 percent, 40 basis points lower compared to its Wednesday's close.
The call market ramained range-bound in thin activity, dealers said. Call opened at 0.25-0.75 percent and closed at 0.10-0.25 percent, dealers said.
